Topic: What to Ask First in a Psychiatric Interview
Exact Hook: Do not start a psychiatric interview randomly.
Full Voiceover Script: Start with the patient’s chief concern in their own words. Then clarify onset, duration, and current severity. Next, identify how the problem is affecting daily function. Before going too far, screen for immediate safety concerns. A structured beginning makes the rest of the interview clearer, faster, and safer.
Exact On-Screen Text: Start with chief concern Clarify onset, duration, severity Assess function Screen safety early
Canva Visual Direction: Notebook or desk scene. Use a clean four-step interview flow graphic. Animate each step appearing one by one.

Topic: The Difference Between Mood and Affect
Exact Hook: Students often confuse mood with affect.
Full Voiceover Script: Mood is the patient’s sustained emotional experience. Affect is the emotional expression you observe. Mood is reported. Affect is seen. If a patient says they feel depressed, but appears smiling and reactive, affect may be incongruent with mood. This distinction matters in both assessment and documentation.
Exact On-Screen Text: Mood = reported feeling Affect = observed expression Congruent vs incongruent
Canva Visual Direction: Split-screen style comparison. Left side: mood definition. Right side: affect definition. Finish with one short charting example.

Topic: One SOAP Note Mistake That Weakens Good Assessments
Exact Hook: One SOAP note mistake makes good assessments sound unclear.
Full Voiceover Script: A common mistake is mixing subjective and objective data. If the patient reports hopelessness, that belongs in subjective. If you observe tearfulness, slowed speech, or poor eye contact, that belongs in objective. Strong notes separate reported experience from observed findings. That is what makes your reasoning easier to trust.
Exact On-Screen Text: Subjective = patient reports Objective = clinician observes Separate them clearly
Canva Visual Direction: Show Subjective and Objective as two clean columns. Place examples under each.
Approved CTA: Save this for your next SOAP note.

Topic: How to Ask About Suicidal Ideation Clearly
Exact Hook: You do not need awkward wording to ask about suicide.
Full Voiceover Script: Use clear and direct language. Ask whether the patient has had thoughts of wanting to die or thoughts of killing themselves. Then clarify intent, plan, and access to means. Also ask about past attempts and protective factors. Direct questions improve clarity. Vague questions increase risk.
Exact On-Screen Text: Ask directly Clarify intent Clarify plan Clarify means Ask about past attempts
Canva Visual Direction: Minimal checklist animation. Clinical note card or structured prompt list. No dramatic imagery.

Topic: If Your MSE Feels Scattered, Use This Structure
Exact Hook: If your Mental Status Exam feels scattered, use this structure.
Full Voiceover Script: Think in categories, not chaos. Start with appearance and behavior. Then speech and motor activity. Then mood and affect. Then thought process, thought content, and perception. Finish with cognition, insight, and judgment. A category-based approach makes the MSE easier to remember and easier to write.
Exact On-Screen Text: Appearance / behavior Speech / motor Mood / affect Thought process / content / perception Cognition / insight / judgment
Canva Visual Direction: Grid layout with each MSE domain appearing in sequence.

Topic: Why Good Students Still Freeze in Psychiatric Interviews
Exact Hook: Many students do not freeze because they lack knowledge.
Full Voiceover Script: They freeze because they do not yet have a repeatable structure. Knowing symptoms is not the same as knowing what to ask next. A structured interview reduces mental overload. It gives you sequence, direction, and clinical focus. Confidence often improves after structure improves.
Exact On-Screen Text: Knowledge is not enough Structure reduces overload Sequence improves confidence
Canva Visual Direction: Desk setup with overlay text. Use a simple symptoms versus structure contrast graphic.

Topic: Thought Process Is Not Thought Content
Exact Hook: Thought process is not the same as thought content.
Full Voiceover Script: Thought process describes how ideas are organized. Is the patient linear, tangential, circumstantial, or disorganized? Thought content describes what the patient is thinking about. For example, delusions, obsessions, guilt, or suicidal ideation. If you confuse the two, your MSE becomes less precise.
Exact On-Screen Text: Thought process = how thoughts are organized Thought content = what thoughts are about
Canva Visual Direction: Two-column comparison with short examples.

Topic: Do Not Jump to One Diagnosis Too Early
Exact Hook: Do not jump to one diagnosis too early.
Full Voiceover Script: Start with the syndrome pattern first. Look at the major symptom clusters. Then compare time course, severity, impairment, and rule-outs. Only after that should you rank likely differentials. Diagnostic reasoning is comparison. It is not guesswork.
Exact On-Screen Text: Start with syndrome pattern Compare symptom clusters Check time course and impairment Rank differentials
Canva Visual Direction: Step ladder or staircase visual.
Approved CTA: Save this for case study practice.

Topic: Stop Writing Vague Psych Notes
Exact Hook: Stop writing vague psych notes.
Full Voiceover Script: Vague notes weaken clinical credibility. Instead of writing “patient seems off,” describe what you observed. For example: tearful, guarded, slowed speech, poor eye contact, or tangential thought process. Strong documentation is based on observable findings, not fuzzy impressions.
Exact On-Screen Text: Avoid vague wording Use observable findings Write what you saw
Canva Visual Direction: Before-and-after text examples. Use a simple correction format.

Topic: The Functional Impairment Question You Should Not Skip
Exact Hook: Symptoms matter. Functional impairment matters too.
Full Voiceover Script: Always ask how symptoms are affecting work, school, relationships, or self-care. A symptom list alone is not enough. Functional impairment helps determine clinical significance and diagnostic weight. Without it, your formulation may stay incomplete.
Exact On-Screen Text: Work School Relationships Self-care Impairment changes meaning

Topic: What Belongs in the Subjective Section
Exact Hook: The subjective section is not a dumping ground.
Full Voiceover Script: Use the subjective section for what the patient reports. That includes symptoms, duration, severity, triggers, and relevant quotes. Do not place your observations there. If you saw poor eye contact or psychomotor slowing, that belongs in objective. Clean separation improves note quality.
Exact On-Screen Text: Subjective = patient report Symptoms Duration Severity Triggers
Canva Visual Direction: Simple belongs here / not here slide sequence.

Topic: What New Clinicians Miss in Psychiatric Interviews
Exact Hook: The problem is often not lack of knowledge. It is missed structure.
Full Voiceover Script: New clinicians often miss four things. Timeline. Functional impairment. Early safety screening. And substance contribution. When these are missed, the interview may sound organized but still remain incomplete.
Exact On-Screen Text: Timeline Functional impairment Safety early Substance contribution
Canva Visual Direction: Four-part checklist with subtle transitions.

Topic: How to Write a Better Assessment Section
Exact Hook: The assessment section should explain your reasoning.
Full Voiceover Script: Start by summarizing the core symptom picture. Then connect the findings to your most likely diagnosis. Mention important differentials briefly when relevant. Avoid unsupported conclusions. The assessment section is where clinical reasoning becomes visible.
Exact On-Screen Text: Summarize symptoms Connect findings to diagnosis Mention key differentials Avoid unsupported conclusions
Canva Visual Direction: Use a three-step reasoning diagram ending in assessment.

Topic: A Simple Way to Remember the MSE
Exact Hook: Use categories, not chaos.
Full Voiceover Script: When remembering the MSE, stop thinking in long paragraphs. Think in categories. Appearance. Speech. Mood and affect. Thought process and thought content. Perception. Cognition. Insight and judgment. A system is easier to remember than a list.
Exact On-Screen Text: Appearance Speech Mood / affect Thought process / content Perception Cognition Insight / judgment
Canva Visual Direction: One category appears at a time, then the full system appears.

Topic: Why Random Questioning Weakens Interviews
Exact Hook: Random questioning makes psychiatric interviews weaker.
Full Voiceover Script: When questions are asked without structure, important data gets missed. The interview becomes harder to follow. And your documentation becomes harder to organize. A better sequence is chief concern, symptom analysis, safety, history, substance use, psychosocial context, and mental status exam. Structure protects clarity.
Exact On-Screen Text: Chief concern Symptom analysis Safety History Substance use Psychosocial context MSE
Canva Visual Direction: Horizontal flow map with clear arrows.

Topic: One Documentation Habit That Reduces Trust
Exact Hook: One documentation habit weakens otherwise good notes.
Full Voiceover Script: Do not write conclusions without evidence. If you document that the patient is manic, psychotic, or severely depressed, make sure the note shows the findings that support it. Observed speech, affect, thought content, behavior, and symptom pattern should all support your conclusion. Strong charting shows evidence, not labels alone.
Exact On-Screen Text: Do not chart labels only Show supporting findings Evidence builds trust
Canva Visual Direction: Label on one side, supporting evidence on the other.

Topic: A Visual Map for Suicide Risk Questioning
Exact Hook: A visual map makes suicide risk questioning clearer.
Full Voiceover Script: Think in sequence. Ideation. Intent. Plan. Means. Past attempts. Protective factors. When the logic is visible, the questioning becomes clearer and the documentation becomes stronger.
Exact On-Screen Text: Ideation Intent Plan Means Past attempts Protective factors

Topic: Knowing the Case Is Not the Same as Writing the Note
Exact Hook: Knowing the case is not the same as knowing how to write it.
Full Voiceover Script: Many learners understand the patient, but still struggle when the SOAP note is blank. That is usually a structure problem, not an intelligence problem. A documentation framework helps organize what belongs in subjective, objective, assessment, and plan. Clear structure reduces charting paralysis.
Exact On-Screen Text: Understand the case Organize the note Use structure Reduce charting paralysis

Topic: What Makes a Psychiatric Assessment Feel Complete
Exact Hook: A complete assessment feels connected, not crowded.
Full Voiceover Script: A strong psychiatric assessment includes a clear presenting problem, structured symptom review, safety evaluation, relevant history, mental status findings, diagnostic reasoning, and a plan linked to the findings. Completeness does not come from writing more. It comes from organizing the right parts.
Exact On-Screen Text: Presenting problem Symptom review Safety History MSE Reasoning Plan
